body: Forward test of the promise-tracker credibility method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.68 (naive base rate 0.55) that: Marico FY27 consolidated EBITDA grows ≥24% YoY. Evidence: Q2 FY27 call (Nov-2026): revenue +13%, India volume +10%, international +13% cc; EBITDA +27%, margin +200 bps to 18.2%. Guidance raised (second upgrade): 'mid-twenties EBITDA growth up from around 20%'; CFO: 'mid-20s about in the range of 24%, 25% on the minimum side'; revenue 'teens' growth, crossing ₹15,000 cr; margin +120–150 bps for the year. Company notes teens+ revenue growth in 8 of last 10 quarters. Reasoning: Marico has upgraded twice and frames 24–25% as a minimum, with H1 above it (EBITDA +27% in Q2). Copra/input deflation tailwind and operating leverage support it; risk is A&P reinvestment in H2. Resolution: YES if Marico's consolidated EBITDA for FY27 ÷ FY26 − 1 ≥ 24.0%, using the company's reported EBITDA (Q4 FY27 information update/press release); else screener Operating Profit FY27 vs FY26. Source: Marico Q4 FY27 information update / press release; screener.in annual P&L. Resolve by 2027-05-31; score with Brier vs base rate.

body: Forward test of the sector cycle/lead indicator method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.35 (naive base rate 0.50) that: ExxonMobil's Q4 2026 adjusted (non-GAAP) EPS is ≥$4.23 (at or above Q3 2026). Evidence: Q3 2026 release (30-Oct-2026): earnings $15.4bn ($3.72/share), adjusted earnings $17.5bn ($4.23/share), CFO $25.7bn, FCF $19.1bn; announced 2027 buybacks of $20bn; Q4 dividend $1.07. Lead indicators (Yahoo futures, daily closes): Brent averaged $91.50 in Q3 and $103.07 Q4-to-date (to 20-Nov) but has fallen to ~$92.6; NYMEX 3-2-1 crack proxy (2×RBOB+1×HO vs 3×Brent) ~$60/bbl in Q3 vs ~$45/bbl Q4-to-date; Henry Hub $2.89 → $3.06. Reasoning: Sector-cycle lead-indicator test: upstream gains from higher average Brent are likely more than offset by the ~25% fall in refining cracks (XOM is the largest US refiner), and Brent is already back near Q3 levels with six weeks left. Seasonal Q4 items (year-end asset/tax adjustments) add noise but are excluded from adjusted EPS. Resolution: YES if ExxonMobil's Q4 2026 earnings excluding identified items per share (company-defined non-GAAP adjusted EPS) is ≥$4.23. Source: ExxonMobil Q4 2026 earnings release (8-K, EDGAR). Resolve by 2027-02-15; score with Brier vs base rate.
